title: Exactness of inverse image on abelian sheaves and modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. The induced inverse-image functor on sheaves of abelian groups is exact. If $\mathcal B$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, the transported functor on sheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with scalars transported along $f^{-1}\mathcal B$, is exact on underlying abelian sheaves and therefore preserves the finite limits and cokernels used in the free-module relation presentation.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first assertion and proof (underlying inverse image of abelian sheaves is exact); the module assertion here uses transported scalars, not tensoring with a different ring.

proof.text: Put $L=f^{-1}$ and $R=f_*$. By the geometric-morphism definition, $L\dashv R$ and $L$ preserves finite limits. The right-adjoint limit theorem gives preservation of finite products by $R$. Identify abelian sheaves with abelian group objects of the set-sheaf categories using the algebraic-structures equivalence. Apply the abelian-group-object adjunction theorem: it supplies $L_{\rm Ab}\dashv R_{\rm Ab}$, with underlying functors $L,R$ and operations obtained by applying them to addition, zero and negation through the product and terminal comparison isomorphisms. This is precisely the induced inverse image in the statement, and uses no presentation of $f$ by a functor of sites.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, proof of (2); Tag 0038, categories-lemma-adjoint-exact for the right adjoint

proof.text: Finite limits of abelian sheaves are sectionwise limits, by the sheafification-exactness node (1). Their underlying sets are the compatible tuples in the product of the section groups, hence are the sectionwise limits of the underlying sets; the set-sheaf limit theorem identifies these with limits of set sheaves. Apply $L$ to a finite limiting cone of abelian sheaves. Its underlying cone is limiting because $L$ preserves finite limits. For any cone of abelian sheaves to this image diagram, the unique underlying set-sheaf factorization preserves addition: composing the two proposed addition maps with each limiting projection gives the same map, since the cone maps and projections are additive. Joint uniqueness in the limit proves equality. The same argument for zero and negation proves that the factorization is a morphism of abelian sheaves. Its uniqueness follows from underlying uniqueness. Thus $L_{\rm Ab}$ preserves finite limits.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first paragraph of proof, expanded via Sites Tag 00YV and sectionwise limits

proof.text: The lifted adjunction of step 1 and the left-adjoint colimit theorem show that $L_{\rm Ab}$ preserves every existing small colimit, in particular finite colimits and cokernels. Together with step 2, this proves exactness in the finite-limit/finite-colimit sense. Abelian sheaves form abelian categories, so this also preserves exact sequences: the image of a map $a$ is $\ker(\operatorname{coker}a)$, both operations are preserved, and the equality of that image with the next kernel is preserved. Additivity follows from the transported addition: for $a,b:M\to N$, the identity $a+b=+_N\circ\langle a,b\rangle$ is carried by $L$ to the same identity with $L_{\rm Ab}a,L_{\rm Ab}b$.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first assertion; Sites Tag 00YV(2); Categories Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact

proof.text: Let $B=\mathcal B$ and $M$ be a $B$-module sheaf. Its scalar action is a map $\mu:B\times M\to M$ of set sheaves by the naturality required in the module definition. Give $LB$ its transported ring operations, and give $LM$ the action $L(\mu)\circ p_{B,M}^{-1}$, where $p_{B,M}:L(B\times M)\xrightarrow{\sim}LB\times LM$ is the product comparison. Apply $L$ to the diagrams for distributivity in both variables, associativity of the action and the unit law. After the canonical finite-product comparisons these are exactly the module-axiom diagrams for this action. The same argument for the linearity diagram of a module map shows that its image under $L$ is $LB$-linear; identities and composition follow from functoriality. This constructs the transported module functor $T$. Its underlying abelian sheaf has exactly the addition, zero and negation of $L_{\rm Ab}M$, so, writing $V_B,V_{LB}$ for scalar forgetting, $V_{LB}T\cong L_{\rm Ab}V_B$ naturally, also on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, statement and its two-line product-comparison proof; Sites Tag 00YV, ring-structure paragraph

proof.text: Scalar forgetting preserves all small limits and colimits, by the module-sheaf forgetful theorem. It also reflects isomorphisms: the sectionwise inverse of a bijective linear map is linear, because if $v=\alpha(u)$ then $\alpha^{-1}(rv)=\alpha^{-1}(\alpha(ru))=ru$; inverses commute with restrictions by the inverse equations. For a finite module diagram $D$ with limit $P$, the canonical comparison $T(P)\to\lim T(D)$ becomes under $V_{LB}$ the isomorphism $L_{\rm Ab}(\lim V_BD)\to\lim L_{\rm Ab}(V_BD)$ of step 2. Hence the module comparison is an isomorphism. For a finite colimit $Q$, the comparison $\operatorname{colim}T(D)\to T(Q)$ similarly becomes the isomorphism of step 3, and is itself an isomorphism. Thus $T$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits, including cokernels. By the natural identification in step 4 its effect on underlying abelian sheaves is exact as well. The module categories are abelian, and their forgetful functors preserve kernels and cokernels, so the image-as-kernel-of-cokernel argument of step 3 proves preservation of exact sequences of modules. This applies to the cokernel of any free-module relation map. Throughout the target ring is $LB=f^{-1}\mathcal B$ itself.

Step 4: the 03D2 action transport L(mu)∘p^{-1} is written out; the transport of LB's ring axioms is stated briefly but is the same elementary argument. Step 5: forgetting scalars preserves limits and colimits and reflects isomorphisms (proved in the step), so the module comparison maps are isomorphisms. Edge cases checked: identity morphism, zero ring, empty diagram, B=Z, non-flat ring change. No new nodes.
